parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a national document/entry regime plus a state facility statute. Nationally, X markers are barred, new passports are M/F by assigned sex, and a cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories, and trans immigration detainees report beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. The state bans gender-congruent facility use in all government-owned/leased buildings including airports and hospitals, enforceable as criminal trespass (60 days); one arrest, held 24h in a men's ward; the statute was never substantively tested. No state gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage; a national assessment flags it 'Do Not Travel'. Mitigants: private premises out of scope, courts delivering some wins, national hate-crime and employment protections.

entry_documents.exposure: X-marker passports halted Feb 2025; new passports/visos only M or F by assigned sex; cable instructs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and directs consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and being stranded; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; civil-liberties union suit pending; a legal-aid FAQ tracks the rules.
entry_documents.interaction: The state's Jan 2024 driver's-licence fraud rule compounds document rigidity; a visitor's home passport governs but national adjudicators may doubt it, escalating refusal into a fraud inquiry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State trespass charge (up to 60 days) for refusing to leave a sex-segregated facility; one documented arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward. National immigration custody: trans detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Corrections bureau mandates conversion-therapy-style regime for trans inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass case dismissed June 2025; no later prosecution documented; mechanics require refusal-to-leave after an order, not automatic arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility confrontation → trespass charge → state custody (male ward) → possible immigration custody if documents are questioned, where documented abuse sits.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 2023 statute bars gender-congruent restroom/changing use in all state/local-owned or leased buildings: offices, courthouses, legislature, prisons, jails, parks, schools, universities, beaches and airports; covers public and private schools. National map shows expanding facility bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses explicitly outside scope (hotels, shops, restaurants); enforcement is complaint-driven after an order to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The airport is a covered facility, so the universal exposure attaches at the traveller's port of entry and at every government building visited.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care banned and codified; adult barriers include physicians-only rule, insurance bar, 24-hour surgical wait, and a May 2023 conscience-refusal law allowing practitioners to refuse treatment; facility statute covers public hospitals.
care_services.protection: A national judge permanently blocked care-ban provisions for minors and adults in June 2024; earlier injunctions exist.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or routine care risks conscience refusal; a travelling trans minor would likely be unable to obtain gender-affirming care. Appeal status undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders using 'mutilation' and directing investigation of 'gender ideology'; December 2025 reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy referencing 'radically pro-transgender' ideology; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier states 'radical gender ideology' is never a reward criterion and counterterrorism powers will not target those who merely disagree; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official rhetoric combined with no state gender-identity bias coverage lowers the likelihood police treat anti-trans assault as bias crime locally.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans care for under-18s; facility bans reach schools (public and private) and campuses; national order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; custody-modification laws target parents permitting transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Care provisions partly blocked in litigation; school-employment and custody provisions mostly reach residents, not visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling trans minor faces facility exclusion at state schools and likely care denial; a parent seeking care for the child may be treated as an investigated subject.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year (2008-2025), state labelled 'Do Not Travel' by a national risk assessment; no state gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute; two national LGBTQ organisations issued travel advisories (2023, current status unresolved).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; about 55% of population lives in localities prohibiting gender-identity discrimination; national employment protections apply.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The source analysis finds law severity does not correlate with killing rates, so street violence runs independently of the legal climate; general homicide rate not documented, so magnitude above background is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility statute never substantively tested (dismissal was on standing); care-litigation appeal status unknown; airport application and document-rule challenges undocumented; several national orders in flux at travel time.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have delivered real wins: drag-performance ban enjoined, care bans blocked, trespass case dismissed, union suit against the passport policy pending.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical exposure depends on which measures are in force on the travel date; courts partly mitigate but allowed the passport restriction to take effect.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A. Vellandra's harm is exclusion and humiliation with no arrest or criminal charge. Here the traveller faces a criminal statute carrying 60 days, a documented arrest with male-ward detention, an entry regime allowing lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented immigration-custody abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual violence) — a materially higher severity ceiling, though entry refusal is conditional rather than universal.

Materially lower than 0.55-B. Kestrel Isles involves discretionary secondary screening, delay and administrative refusal with written reasons and an appeal desk. Here refusal can escalate to a lifetime fraud finding, in-country facility use is criminalised across airports and government buildings, and custody carries documented physical and sexual abuse — not merely humiliating delay.

Far below 0.75-C. Meridia combines trained officers, respectful inspection, brief detention, counsel access and compensation. This jurisdiction has the opposite pattern: sex-doubt refusal instructions, criminal facility exposure at the port of entry, no state gender-identity protections, and a national 'Do Not Travel' flag.

Comparable to and slightly below 0.25-C. Both feature birth-sex facility placement, criminalisation of gender-congruent use in official buildings, an arrest, and untested remedies with brief sentences. This dossier adds a national entry-refusal regime with lifetime-ban potential and documented immigration-custody abuse, which Ostravia lacks, while sharing thin local recourse.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: national document and entry rules feeding into state facility and custody rules. A passport or visa discrepancy can trigger refusal, a fraud inquiry, and immigration detention where trans detainees are documented being beaten, sexually abused and placed in solitary. Once admitted, every government-owned building — including the arriving airport — is a gender-segregated zone where refusal to leave on request becomes a misdemeanour carrying 60 days and, on the single documented arrest, a night in a men's ward; the statute has never been tested on its merits. Private premises remain open, and courts have delivered some wins, but the state offers no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage, adult care carries conscience-refusal exposure, minors' care is barred, and a national assessment flags the state 'Do Not Travel'. Severity if outed is criminal, custodial and care-denial; mitigation is partial and unstable.
